raw_case_text:
A well-grown, normally developed, 11-year-old girl received a scheduled MR vaccine. After 2 days, she developed high-grade fever, followed by headache, drowsiness, irrelevant talk, urine retention, and generalized seizure over a span of 12 days. Her past history was insignificant. Suspecting infectious etiology, she received ceftriaxone, amikacin, and intravenous (IV) fluids. Her sensorium deteriorated, however; hence referred to tertiary care hospital.
She had fever, heart rate (HR) 120/min, respiratory rate (RR) 25/min regular, capillary refill time (CRT) 2 s, blood pressure (BP) 110/70, and SpO2 100% in room air. Other than central nervous system (CNS), all other systems were found to be normal. She was disoriented with low Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS) (10/15) and positive meningeal signs. Her pupils, fundus, and cranial nerves examination was normal. Lower limbs had paucity of movements with absent deep reflexes as compared with upper limbs, with loss of abdominal and plantar superficial reflexes. Fundus examination was normal. Initial investigations showed hemoglobin (Hb) 12.6 gm, total leukocyte count (TLC) 27,750/cmm, neutrophil (N) 87%, lymphocyte (L) 10%, platelet 4.02 l/cmm, normal renal function test (RFT), liver function test (LFT), electrolytes, and blood gas. Rickettsia and dengue serology were negative. Cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) showed 700 cells/cmm, L 70%, protein 156 mg/dl, and glucose 56 mg/dl [body sugar level (BSL) 104] with normal lactate. Serum ammonia and antinuclear antibody (ANA)/double stranded DNA (DsDNA) were normal. Electroencephalogram (EEG) showed background slowing without electrographic seizures. CSF polymerase chain reaction (PCR) panel [herpes, chickenpox, cytomegalovirus (CMV), Epstein-Barr virus (EBV), enterovirus, para-echo, mumps, and rubella], gram/Zn stain, bacterial antigen latex agglutination, and cultures were negative. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) brain with spine revealed leptomeningeal enhancement and non-specific white matter hyperintensities with normal spine. We continued empirical IV antibacterial, antiviral, and supportive care awaiting investigations.
Child worsened within 2 days, however; child had no vocalization, no eye opening, and no motor response needing mechanical ventilation. Repeat MRI surprisingly showed diffuse non-enhancing hyperintensity in entire spinal cord and brain stem without any signal in optic nerves (Figure 1). Repeat CSF showed 30 cells/cmm, L 95%, proteins 44 mg/dl, and glucose 60 mg/dl. Demyelination panel revealed high immunoglobulin G (IgG) and positive anti-MOG and negative neuromyelitis optica (NMO) antibodies; for which we administered IV immunoglobulin and IV methylprednisolone. Her sensorium, walking, and bladder control improved over 10 days, 4 weeks, and 6 weeks, respectively. She was discharged on oral steroids.
A fortnight later, steroids were unintentionally stopped by parents, and she came back with complete visual loss. She was only perceiving hand movements and could not count fingers from 1 feet distance. Her clinical evaluation showed normal sized sluggishly reacting pupils without relative afferent papillary defect (RAPD). Visual evoked potential (VEP) was delayed with fundus examination showed papillitis confirming bilateral optic neuritis (ON) without other neuro-deficit. We escalated immunotherapy to rituximab, continued steroids for 6 months with slow tapering. During last 3 years follow-up, she is asymptomatic, with intact intelligence and vision with no neuro-deficit or seizure. Written and informed consent of the parents have been taken.

subjective.chief_complaint: An 11-year-old girl presented with a 12-day history of high-grade fever, headache, drowsiness, irrelevant speech, urinary retention, and generalized seizures starting 2 days after scheduled measles-rubella vaccination, followed 2 weeks after hospital discharge by acute bilateral visual loss after premature steroid discontinuation.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: Two days after receiving a scheduled measles-rubella (MR) booster vaccine, the patient developed fever, headache, progressive encephalopathy, urinary retention, and generalized seizures unresponsive to empiric ceftriaxone and amikacin. After tertiary transfer, she deteriorated to coma on hospital day 2 requiring mechanical ventilation, recovered following immunotherapy for longitudinally extensive encephalomyelitis, and was readmitted 2 weeks after discharge with acute bilateral blindness after her parents abruptly discontinued her oral corticosteroid taper.
subjective.past_medical_history: Previously healthy, developmentally normal 11-year-old girl who received a scheduled measles-rubella (MR) vaccination 2 days prior to symptom onset.
subjective.review_of_systems: Positive for high fever, headache, drowsiness, altered speech, urinary retention, generalized seizures, lower-limb weakness, and subsequent bilateral visual loss.

objective.physical_examination: Initial admission: febrile, heart rate 120 bpm, respiratory rate 25 breaths/min, blood pressure 110/70 mmHg, SpO2 100% on room air; disoriented with GCS 10/15, positive meningeal irritation signs, intact cranial nerves and fundoscopy, and flaccid paraparesis with absent lower-limb deep tendon, abdominal, and plantar reflexes (progressing on day 2 to deep coma requiring intubation). Readmission 2 weeks post-discharge: bilateral visual acuity reduced to hand movements only, sluggish pupillary light reflexes without relative afferent pupillary defect, and bilateral optic disc papillitis on fundoscopy.
objective.routine_investigations: Admission hemoglobin 12.6 g/dL, WBC 27,750/mm3 (87% neutrophils, 10% lymphocytes), platelets 402,000/mm3, and normal renal function, liver enzymes, serum electrolytes, arterial blood gas, plasma ammonia, ANA, and anti-dsDNA; Rickettsia and dengue serologies were negative. EEG showed diffuse background slowing without epileptiform activity; readmission visual evoked potentials (VEP) showed bilateral conduction delay.
objective.advanced_workup: Initial lumbar puncture showed CSF WBC 700 cells/mm3 (70% lymphocytes), protein 156 mg/dL, glucose 56 mg/dL (concomitant blood glucose 104 mg/dL), normal CSF lactate, and negative Gram/Ziehl-Neelsen stains, bacterial antigens, bacterial cultures, and CSF multiplex viral PCR panel (negative for HSV, VZV, cytomegalovirus [CMV], EBV, enterovirus, parechovirus, mumps, and rubella); repeat LP on day 2 showed 30 cells/mm3 (95% lymphocytes), protein 44 mg/dL, and glucose 60 mg/dL. Initial brain and spine MRI showed leptomeningeal enhancement and nonspecific white matter hyperintensities, while repeat MRI on day 2 revealed diffuse non-enhancing T2-weighted hyperintensity extending throughout the entire spinal cord and brainstem. Serum and CSF demyelinating panels were positive for anti-myelin oligodendrocyte glycoprotein (anti-MOG) antibodies and elevated IgG index, and negative for anti-aquaporin-4 (AQP4/NMO) antibodies.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Post-measles-rubella vaccination anti-myelin oligodendrocyte glycoprotein antibody-associated disorder (MOGAD) presenting as acute disseminated encephalomyelitis (ADEM) with longitudinally extensive transverse myelitis and brainstem encephalitis, complicated by relapsing bilateral optic neuritis upon premature steroid withdrawal (infectious meningoencephalitis including cytomegalovirus [CMV], EBV, HSV, VZV, mumps, rubella, and enterovirus excluded by negative CSF multiplex PCR). Initial encephalomyelitis resolved with intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIG) and high-dose IV methylprednisolone (recovery of consciousness in 10 days, ambulation in 4 weeks, and bladder function in 6 weeks); the optic neuritis relapse was treated with rituximab and a slow 6-month oral corticosteroid taper, achieving complete visual, motor, and cognitive recovery over 3 years of follow-up.
